newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Optus says looks at float options.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Optus says looks at float options.

text.p: Australia's second largest telecommunications carrier, Optus Communications Pty Ltd said on Thursday its shareholders were examining alternative strategies to proceed with the flotation of the company after a court decision which could potentially delay its planned float.
"Shareholders are investigating alternative strategies for proceeding with the float of Optus Communications," a spokeswoman from Optus told Reuters.

The official statement followed the handing down of interim direction from the New South Wales Supreme Court in a legal dispute involving Seven Network Ltd and Optus' 46.5 percent owned pay television subsidiary, Optus Vision.

Analysts said the dispute, which centres on the relationship between Optus Vision and two of its shareholders, Publishing and Braodcasting Ltd and Continental Cable vision of the U.S., could delay the Optus float, planned for later this year.

"It appears that it will certainly delay the float on the assumption that the directors cannot sign off the prospectus, until that particular matter has been heard," one Sydney-based telecommunications analyst said.
The analyst said as the dispute involved secret agreements between the parties, it was difficult to predict the likely outcome.
"I get a feeling from Optus that they have a couple of things up their sleeve they have to pull out yet," the said.
The analyst said Seven could use the dispute as a bargaining chip for an out of court settlement.
"One of the theories here is that Seven are trying to negotiate their way into a non-exclusive deal, because at the moment they are locked in," he said.
"All of this must be sorted out to sign off the prospectus as Optus Vision is a very important part of Optus Communications," he added.
Optus is 25 percent owned by Mayne Nickless Ltd and 24.5 percent each by BellSouth Corp of the United States and Cable and Wireless Plc of Britain.
Mayne Nickless has said it would sell its 25 percent stake into the Optus float, giving its existing shareholders entitlements to the issue.
Dealers said Mayne Nickless shares had been under pressure earlier this week due to uncertainty about the Optus float.
Mayne Nickless shares closed two cents higher at A$8.28 on Thursday after touching an intra-day low of A$8.10.
